source_caption:
📺 Dr. Ken (2015–2017)

Dr. Ken follows Dr. Ken Park, a talented but sarcastic physician who struggles to balance his demanding medical career with the responsibilities of being a husband and father. Despite his intelligence and professional experience, Ken’s unconventional approach to medicine and lack of bedside manners frequently create hilarious situations at work. At home, he relies on his supportive wife, Allison, a successful therapist, while attempting to raise their teenage daughter, Molly, and eccentric young son, Dave. Between dealing with difficult patients, workplace disagreements, parenting challenges, and complicated family relationships, Ken constantly finds himself in awkward and entertaining situations. Although his methods are often questionable, his genuine love for his family and dedication to his patients remain at the heart of his character. Starring Ken Jeong, Suzy Nakamura, and Tisha Campbell, the series delivers relatable comedy, heartwarming moments, and entertaining storytelling about marriage, parenthood, cultural identity, friendship, and balancing professional and personal life.

🎭 Genre: Comedy • Family • Medical Sitcom

⭐ IMDb: 5.7/10

⏱️ Runtime: Approximately 22 minutes per episode • TV-PG

🎥 Creators: Ken Jeong, Jared Stern & Mike O’Connell

📺 Seasons: 2 • 44 Episodes

📚 Inspired By: Ken Jeong’s real-life experiences as a physician before becoming a comedian and actor.

📺 Where to Watch: Check Amazon Prime Video and Apple TV for current streaming or purchase availability in the United States.

source_details.synopsis: Dr. Ken is an American multi-camera sitcom that aired on ABC from October 2, 2015, to March 31, 2017. The series was created, written, and co-executive produced by its lead actor, Ken Jeong, who based the concept on his experience as a physician prior to becoming a stand-up comedian. The series is an ABC Studios/Sony Pictures Television co-production. On October 20, 2015, ABC ordered a full season of 22 episodes for the first season. On May 12, 2016, the series was renewed for a second season, which premiered on September 23, 2016. On May 11, 2017, ABC cancelled the series after two seasons.
